note: How long each bridge waits on Ethereum before acting on a message or deposit, by default, and the one setting that moves it to FCR. None reads Ethereum's safe block by default today. Re-checked 3 Nov 2026 (on-chain reads at block ~26.33M where noted). Intent bridges (Across, Relay) are "variable": each filler sets its own wait.

bridges.name: Across
bridges.switchTitle: Fill at `safe` instead of by deposit size
bridges.switch: The reference relayer counts 2 to 33 blocks depending on the deposit's size, set in `MIN_DEPOSIT_CONFIRMATIONS`. Replace the count with a check that the deposit's block is at or below `safe`.

bridges.name: LayerZero
bridges.switch: Every default Ethereum route waits 15 confirmations before the DVNs verify a message. Apps can already set their own count; a DVN that checks the block is at or below `safe` replaces the count with FCR.
bridges.source: LayerZero default config API, all Ethereum routes; SendUln302 read on-chain

bridges.name: Wormhole
bridges.lede: Wormhole already has a Safe level. FCR makes it fast: Guardians read `safe` from their own Ethereum nodes.
bridges.switch: The Token Bridge uses finalized today. Guardians already honour level 201, Ethereum's `safe` block. With FCR on the Guardians' nodes, that block is seconds old instead of minutes.
bridges.source: Token Bridge finality() read on-chain; Wormhole consistency levels

bridges.name: Hyperlane
bridges.switch: Validators sign Ethereum checkpoints 15 blocks behind the head. `reorgPeriod` already takes a block tag (BSC and Polygon use `finalized`), so moving to FCR is a change in the registry's `chains/ethereum/metadata.yaml`.

bridges.name: Chainlink CCIP
bridges.lede: No node to run: Chainlink’s node operators read Ethereum. Two switches, in order.

steps.title: Chainlink enables the safe flag
steps.body: CCIP 2.0 has a faster-than-finality mode that can wait for Ethereum’s `safe` block, the block FCR confirms. It is live on testnet; Chainlink switches it on for each mainnet lane.

steps.title: You opt in
steps.body: As the token pool owner, call `setAllowedFinalityConfig` with `WAIT_FOR_SAFE_FLAG` (`0x00010000`). Senders then ask for it per transfer; everything else keeps waiting for finality.

steps.title: Cap and fund the rare reorg
steps.body: A transfer released at `safe` could be undone if Ethereum reorgs that block, leaving tokens minted on the other side without their lock or burn. Give these transfers their own rate limit (`setRateLimitConfig` with `fastFinality: true`) and a fee (`fastFinalityTransferFeeBps`) to cover that risk, and keep finality for large transfers.

bridges.name: Axelar
bridges.switch: Validators wait for Ethereum's `finalized` block, falling back to 200 confirmations. Reading `safe` from a node with FCR is a change in vald's Ethereum client.

bridges.name: Circle CCTP
bridges.lede: Only Circle can switch it on: its own service decides when a burn on Ethereum is attested.
bridges.switch: Standard Transfers wait for finality, about 65 blocks. Fast Transfer already attests after 2 blocks, but it is paid and capped by an allowance. With FCR, Standard Transfers could be attested in seconds, backed by attestations instead of a block count.
bridges.fast: Fast Transfer (opt-in, paid): 2 blocks, about 20 s

bridges.name: deBridge
bridges.switch: Validators sign a message after 12 confirmations on Ethereum. DLN orders are separate: takers choose their own wait, 12 blocks in the reference taker.

bridges.name: Stargate
bridges.lede: Stargate inherits LayerZero's wait: its pools require 4 DVNs that each count 15 blocks.
bridges.switchTitle: Ask the required DVNs to confirm at `safe`
bridges.switch: Stargate's pools use LayerZero's 15-block confirmation on Ethereum, for Taxi and Bus alike. Once its DVNs confirm at `safe`, the pools' config can drop the count.
bridges.source: Stargate USDC pool config read on-chain via LayerZero SendUln302

bridges.name: Relay
bridges.source: Relay docs: solvers fill before settlement and set their own wait

bridges.name: Socket
bridges.switch: Socket's messaging layer waits 6 confirmations on Ethereum. Bungee routes inherit the wait of the bridge they use.

bridges.name: Connext
bridges.lede: Connext is in legacy mode; its successor, Everclear, settles over its own Hyperlane deployment.
bridges.switch: The fast path waits 7 confirmations on Ethereum; the slow path 30 to 60 minutes.
